subject: CAIQ/CSA claim pack assembly request from Norstar Procurement
messages:
From: Maya Singh <security@norstarhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@norstarhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ control mapping & evidence pull for Norstar procurement

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the overview yesterday. Procurement needs a CAIQ-style crosswalk for our purchase review. Can you provide: 
- A filled CAIQ template (we attached ours) with your control assertions (implemented/partial/none)
- For each implemented control, one canonical artifact (log excerpt, config screenshot, runbook page, or signed attestation)
- A short note on scope (hosted API vs dedicated vs private) and data residency for any EU-scoped controls

We are looking to complete vendor review by Dec 9. If you can get an initial claim pack by Nov 30 that would keep us on schedule.

Attached: Norstar_CAIQ_template.xlsx (they sent this).

Appreciate it — let me know if you prefer a short working call.

Best,
Maya Singh
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Norstar Health

--
Attachment: Norstar_CAIQ_template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <security@norstarhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control mapping & evidence pull for Norstar procurement

Maya — thanks for the clear ask. We'll take this on. Quick plan: 

1) Scope confirmation: are you validating Hosted API only, or do you need Dedicated/Private variants? The evidence differs for private deployments (on-prem boundary diagrams, KMS keys).
2) Deliverables by Nov 30 (initial): completed CAIQ sheet with assertions + one artifact per implemented control for top 30 controls you flagged in column G.
3) Dec 6–9: follow-up package with additional artifacts and runtime log excerpts for sampling.

Kimberly, can you kick off the artifact pull for the identity/access controls and attach short snippets? Jordan — can you own network/service boundary diagrams and residency notes?

We'll attach a small set of files to the first pass. If you want a 30-minute go/no-go on Nov 29, we can set time.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Cloud Compliance (on rotation)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (none from us yet)

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control mapping & evidence pull for Norstar procurement

Thanks Aditya — I've started pulling artifacts. Attached are three starter items and a short interpretation note for two controls Maya highlighted.

Quick highlights: 
- IAM/Key rotation (CCM: ID management family): we have an auth rotation runbook excerpt and the policy enforcement log sample. See auth-rotation-snippet.txt (redacted) and kv-cache-evidence.pdf for token issuance telemetry. The runbook path is /runbooks/auth/rotation.md in our internal repo.
- Service boundary: attached a simplified diagram (service-boundary-diagram.png) showing hosted API surface and Dedicated/Private differences. Hosted API = multi-tenant, no customer KMS; Dedicated + Private = customer-dedicated clusters + optional KMS.
- Evidence approach: we'll mark each CAIQ assertion as Implemented / Partial / NotApplicable and include a pointer to the artifact and a single excerpt PDF where possible.

I'll generate a completed CAIQ sheet by EOD Nov 30 and drop a read-only copy to the shared Drive link. Jordan, if you can confirm the residency note (EU tenancy options) I will include it in the comments column.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: auth-rotation-snippet.txt (text), kv-cache-evidence.pdf (pdf), service-boundary-diagram.png (png)

From: Maya Singh <security@norstarhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@norstarhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control mapping & evidence pull for Norstar procurement

Aditya / Kimberly — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying items from procurement: 

1) For controls where you mark "Partial", can you include the planned remediation or compensating control and an expected ETA? Procurement wants firm dates for exceptions.
2) For hosted API telemetry samples, we need a 7-day slice (not just single-line samples) for the log-based controls (e.g., SI-6 style behaviors). Is that feasible for the Dec 6 package?
3) Please redact any customer-identifying data from log excerpts.

If you can include those three things in the Nov 30 initial drop or clearly call them out with a follow-up ETA, we should be able to keep Dec 9 final review.

I'll take the Nov 29 working call if you set it up.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Norstar Health

--
